title: Module 8: Basic steel design to EC3: laterally restrained beams
shortTitle: Basic steel design to EC3: laterally restrained beams
whyItMatters: This is your Year 1 capstone. It brings together tributary load takedown, ULS/SLS combinations, statics, SFDs/BMDs, section classification, bending, shear, deflection, bearing, restraint detailing, and independent checking into a complete 17-part engineering calculation package.
introduction: Covers the complete design workflow for a laterally restrained simply supported Universal Beam to BS EN 1993-1-1: steel grades and thickness effect on yield strength fy, cross-section classification (Classes 1 to 4), plastic vs elastic bending resistance Mc,Rd, shear area Av and plastic shear resistance Vpl,Rd, high-shear moment interaction awareness, SLS deflection checks, web bearing/buckling, padstone/support detailing, what "laterally restrained" truly requires on site, and the 17-item Capstone Project.
objectives: Select a trial UB section, account for self-weight and thickness-dependent yield strength fy, and understand section classification (Classes 1, 2, 3, and 4).
Calculate cross-section bending resistance Mc,Rd, shear resistance Vpl,Rd, and serviceability deflection for a laterally restrained beam.
Specify practical bearing lengths, padstones, web stiffener awareness, connection assumptions, lateral restraint details, and independent checking items for the 17-item Capstone Project.
learningGate: Explain why the characteristic and design line loads in your calculation note are correct.,Explain physically and practically why the beam is assumed laterally restrained.,State clearly whether bending, shear, or serviceability deflection governs the chosen section.,Explain what the support, padstone, and bearing arrangement physically needs.,Identify what site or design change could make your calculation invalid.,List what must be independently checked before real-world use.

options: It identifies the extent to which local plate buckling of the compression flange or web limits resistance: Classes 1 and 2 reach full plastic moment (W_pl · f_y / γ_M0), Class 3 is limited to first elastic yield at the extreme fibre (W_el,min · f_y / γ_M0), and Class 4 buckles locally in the elastic range (requiring effective modulus W_eff)

questions.learningObjective: Explain why yield strength f_y reduces as plate/flange thickness t increases
questions.prompt: Why do steel product standards (such as BS EN 10025) and Eurocode 3 specify a lower nominal yield strength f_y for thick flanges (e.g. t = 25 mm) than for thin flanges (e.g. t = 12 mm) of an identical steel grade S355?
options: Because the maximum principal tensile stress under pure shear equals the uniaxial yield strength according to the Rankine maximum normal stress hypothesis, which governs brittle fracture in unreinforced cast iron and uncracked plain concrete elements rather than ductile structural steel

Thicker steel plates cool more slowly during hot rolling and experience less mechanical grain refinement through the core thickness, resulting in a coarser grain microstructure with a slightly lower yield strength

Because the elastic shear modulus G is related to Young’s modulus E by G = E / [2(1 + ν)], which introduces a Poisson’s ratio reduction factor across the web depth whenever transverse direct stresses are neglected in simple beam theory

Because Eurocode partial safety factors for resistance incorporate a statistical log-normal coefficient of variation for hot-rolled plate thickness tolerances, mill rolling residual stresses, and out-of-straightness bow imperfections across the member length
questions.explanation: Metallurgical cooling rate and rolling reduction govern grain size (Hall-Petch relationship); always check the governing element thickness t before writing down fy!

questions.learningObjective: Explain why higher yield strength S355 has stricter c/t local buckling limits (ε = 0.81)
questions.prompt: Why can a thin-walled section that is Class 2 in S275 steel become Class 3 in S355 steel?
options: It redistributes the peak hogging bending moment into the adjacent midspan zone through rigid-plastic hinge rotation without requiring supplementary lateral-torsional restraint, web stiffeners, or ductile rotation capacity at the support interface when evaluated under unfactored serviceability actions across the gross cross-section without partial safety factors or second-order geometric slenderness reductions

Because reaching the higher yield stress of S355 (355 N/mm² vs 275 N/mm²) requires a larger compressive yield strain (ε_y = f_y/E) while the elastic plate buckling stiffness E remains unchanged, making local buckling occur earlier relative to yield

It eliminates vertical shear deformation across the web depth by forcing the neutral axis to remain coincident with the geometric centroid of the uncracked transformed section throughout both construction and permanent service stages

questions.learningObjective: Calculate ULS design line load w_Ed for a steel secondary beam to BS EN 1990
questions.prompt: A simply supported steel secondary floor beam spans L = 6.0 m and carries a characteristic permanent line load g_k = 10.0 kN/m (including beam self-weight) and a characteristic variable line load q_k = 12.0 kN/m. Using BS EN 1990 combination equation (6.10) with gamma_G = 1.35 and gamma_Q = 1.50, calculate the total factored design UDL w_Ed in kN/m.
questions.assumptions: 1-way tributary floor span; full continuous lateral restraint provided to top flange by composite deck.
questions.explanation: w_Ed = gamma_G * g_k + gamma_Q * q_k = 1.35 * 10.0 + 1.50 * 12.0 = 13.5 + 18.0 = 31.5 kN/m. Step-by-step verification confirms consistent SI metric units before substitution according to BS EN 1990 Expression 6.10 and UK National Annex.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate maximum midspan design bending moment M_Ed for a simply supported beam
questions.prompt: For the simply supported steel floor beam of span L = 6.0 m carrying the factored design line load w_Ed = 31.5 kN/m along its entire span, calculate the maximum midspan design bending moment M_Ed = w_Ed * L^2 / 8 in kN·m.
questions.assumptions: Simply supported boundary conditions at both ends; beam is laterally restrained against out-of-plane buckling.
questions.explanation: M_Ed = w_Ed * L^2 / 8 = 31.5 * (6.0)^2 / 8 = 31.5 * 36.0 / 8 = 141.75 kN·m. Verified against first-principles beam flexure theory and BS EN 1993-1-1 Cl. 6.2.5.
